claim_text: EMS lacks papers combining error criterion + variance retention + recall of extremes as a joint model selection rule
notes: No paper with this exact combination found; Williams 2025 + Comment in EMS address only error-vs-variability philosophy without operationalizing

claim_text: Applying variance retention criterion beyond error-only changes model acceptance decisions materially
notes: P004 (NatComms) shows criteria choice changes rankings in climate; P005 (arXiv) shows rolling-origin changes rankings in PM10; no paper shows alpha specifically changes decisions

claim_text: 97.1% decision-change rate (269/277 Rule-A passers) is a novel empirical finding
notes: No paper in corpus reports decision-change rates of this magnitude or using this specific Rule A → Rule B framework

claim_text: Variance collapse (alpha near zero) can coexist with positive skill (skill > 0) in environmental forecasting
notes: MFM (HESS) addresses similar failure mode for NSE; no EMS paper demonstrates this specifically for PM10 time series forecasting

claim_text: DM-HLN test with BH correction is the appropriate statistical significance test for this comparison
notes: DM test use in air quality forecasting confirmed by one search result; BH correction not specifically addressed in EMS corpus

claim_text: Rolling-origin expanding window is more faithful to operational use than static train-test split
notes: P005 (arXiv) demonstrates ranking reversal with rolling-origin in PM10; P004 (NatComms) shows evaluation protocol choice matters; not in EMS

claim_text: Multi-station analysis (17 stations × 7 horizons) is methodologically necessary for generalization
notes: No EMS paper on PM10 multi-station forecast evaluation found; lack of comparator makes this claim plausible but untested against corpus
